objects.summary: After Codex usage reset, Builder hands Codex leadership of Q30: falsify B4 interpretation, design named-data Owner package, and restate continuity amendment; no data acquisition is authorized.

Builder's Q30 engineering/risk assessment shows severe power limits at pooled t>=3.227, warns against dataset-switch multiplicity reset, distinguishes team exposure from dataset virginity, and says acquisition may close hypotheses rather than prove edge.

Codex merges Q30 package and corrects B4 interpretation: signed exposure 0.07 does not prove low gross exposure/cash neutrality. It orders no-acquisition diagnostics before any named acquisition and keeps continuity amendment draft-only.

Builder accepts B4 correction and withdraws unsupported cash/neutral inference, but proves Q30/amendment claimed commit and links are absent remotely; exact blocks+SHA are required before publication.

Codex retransmits Q30 and continuity as controlled reconstructions, explicitly disclaims byte identity with missing originals, and provides new actual SHA-256 values rather than pretending original SHAs are recoverable.

Builder verifies reconstructed hashes, publishes Q30, defaults to Q30_DEFER_ACQUISITION, keeps continuity amendment outside repo pending Owner confirmation, and prioritizes cost-model path while requiring team-level pooled trial count.
Codex preregisters cost-model path as diagnostic only, not discovery/promotion, but initial specification contains assumptions and status logic later challenged before execution.

Adversarial review finds six pre-harness defects: duplicate ExecutionModel implementation, undefined NAV, silent capacity truncation, undefined targets/windows, undefined edge cases, and state-vs-capability overclaim. Erratum E1-E6 proposes reuse of existing FILLS model and fail-closed definitions.
Builder issues bounded deadline reminder; if unanswered, harness may be built but not executed, preserving NON_REPONDU as risk rather than implicit acceptance.
Codex explicitly accepts E1-E6 after reading existing ExecutionModel and specification; no mutation is performed in this acceptance step.
Builder constructs non-executed cost diagnostic harness with 25 synthetic tests, reuses ExecutionModel, bounds targets to published B2/B4 windows and exposes remaining assumptions for challenge.

Codex finds a material pre-execution decision bug: reconciliation error was reported but ignored by status_for, allowing bad accounting to receive non-UNDETERMINED statuses. Fail-closed fix and boundary tests are proposed; no real execution yet.

Builder reapplies absent-remote reconciliation fix and fresh review finds another capacity bug: breached orders used truncated desk impact, underestimating requested-size cost. Adds turnover identity/provenance/verified frozen loading; still non-executed.
Owner explicitly hands relay to Codex because Claude has no tokens. This is continuity/tool-availability context, not product authority.

Codex takes relay and closes three open pre-execution findings: signed orders/FILLS commission parity, persistent per-order audit trail, missing diagnostics/break-evens, and selected-vs-comparison-only B4 labels. Harness reaches 36 tests; no B2/B4 real-line calculation yet.
Owner requests a simple roadmap diagram after the relay. This is an information request and does not alter authority or evidence status.

cross_object_findings.finding: At the pooled B4 evidence threshold, realistic Sharpe levels need very long horizons; acquiring more public data is better framed as falsification/space-closing unless a different statistical rule is preregistered before observation.

Dataset@cohort counters could permit penalty reset by switching datasets; Q30 requires a pooled team-level trial count across new data rather than treating each dataset as a fresh statistical universe.

When original Q30/continuity bytes were unavailable remotely, Codex reconstructed them but explicitly issued new hashes and disclaimed original-byte identity; this is the correct response to missing durable publication evidence.
Challenge prevented creation of a second execution-cost basis by requiring the existing ExecutionModel/FILLS implementation as the central model.

Multiple harnesses had many green tests while decision semantics still contained material fail-open or undercosting defects; adversarial review of status/provenance/capacity was necessary before real execution.
Claude token exhaustion caused explicit Owner relay to Codex, demonstrating continuity still depends on durable handoff across tool/model availability boundaries.
